purpose: Doxazosin is used to treat high blood pressure and to help men with an enlarged prostate gland urinate more easily. For blood pressure, it helps lower the force on your blood vessel walls. For the prostate, it relaxes the muscles around the bladder and prostate so urine can flow more freely.
how_it_works: Your body has tiny receptors called alpha-1 receptors in blood vessels and in the muscles around your prostate and bladder. Doxazosin blocks these receptors, which causes the muscles to relax. When blood vessels relax, your blood pressure goes down. When the muscles near your prostate relax, it becomes easier to urinate.
common_side_effects: Dizziness or lightheadedness, especially when you stand up quickly. Feeling tired or drowsy. Headache. Swelling in your ankles or feet. Runny nose. Stomach upset or nausea.
warnings: This medicine can cause a sudden drop in blood pressure when you stand up, which can make you dizzy or faint — this is most common after your first dose or when your dose is increased, so take your first dose at bedtime. Tell your doctor if you plan to have eye surgery, as this medication can affect the procedure. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how it affects you. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, especially other blood pressure medications.
typical_dosing: You usually start with 1 mg taken once a day, often at bedtime to reduce dizziness. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose over several weeks up to a maximum of 8 mg per day for blood pressure, or 8 mg per day for prostate symptoms. The extended-release tablet (Cardura XL) is taken once daily with breakfast and should not be crushed or chewed.
